title: Finite geometric detection of scalar annihilation
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, X a Noetherian scheme, and F a constructible sheaf of Λ-modules on the small étale site of X. Then there are n and points x_i of X such that the intersection of the annihilators of the geometric stalks of F at the algebraic-closure points of x_i is contained in the intersection, over all étale objects U of X, of the annihilators of F(U).

proof.text: Choose the finite constructible stratification [def-constructible-constructible]. Its strata have Noetherian underlying spaces as embedded subspaces of X. The images of an etale trivializing cover of each locally constant restriction [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant] are open and cover the stratum. Compactness gives finitely many members; discard empty members and choose one point on each. Compose with the stratum immersion to obtain a finite list x_i in X.

For each selected member, the algebraic-closure point of x_i lifts through its locally closed stratum and the etale chart. The inverse-image stalk isomorphism identifies its stalk of F with the constant value of that chart. Use the constant-sheaf stalk formula and the natural uliftSheafFiberIso to make this a linear isomorphism. A scalar annihilating the selected stalk therefore annihilates the chart value. Every geometric point of X lifts through its unique stratum and some selected chart, so the scalar annihilates all geometric stalks of F.

The scalar endomorphism of F is zero on every geometric stalk, hence zero by geometric stalk conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. On evaluating at an arbitrary etale object U the scalar kills every section of F(U), and hence belongs to their annihilator intersection. For empty X take n=0: there are no stalk conditions and conservativity forces every scalar endomorphism to be zero. For a zero sheaf all the annihilators are the unit ideal.
